name: f8-secure-growth-v1
idea_origin: playbook:P10 (less defensive family that keeps its response to warnings), chosen because the stall trigger fires and because of the score-gap finding in findings.md (strategy-session request, 26 Oct ~14:45 UTC)
operator: new family seeded from the F3 core (cross-branch hypothesis under the stagnation rule)
hypothesis: Completed games already survive; the score they leave on the table is mostly career level and wealth (findings.md, 48 completed games, all actors), and every family so far optimises survival. F3's Clear state spends quiet quarters lifting the weakest statistic, which keeps the agent safe but does not compete for promotion. A policy that keeps F3's risk response (Secure) and weak-review plan (Repair) with higher precedence, and otherwise plays for promotion and pay (Grow: Apply for a key project, High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials while Health is comfortable, story options that raise Output, Skill, Wealth or standing at a bounded cost), will earn more A or S reviews, hence more promotions and salary, and end with higher level and wealth dimensions than F3 and f3-lean without more eliminations.
change: New family. Reuses f3-lean's turn loop, risk-signal list, Raised/Escalating responses (merged into one Secure mode with Defuse first in the next Energy phase and every Energy phase while signals repeat, story preference for disclose/fix/close, exit after a whole quarter without a new signal) and the weak review plan (Repair). Recovery becomes the first mode. F3's Clear state ('best visible trade-off; lift the weakest statistic') is replaced by Grow. Dropped from f3-lean: Lay low and reduce risk as the Escalating main action (Secure keeps Defuse in Energy, the main action stays with Repair or Grow) and the explicit no-new-commitments clause. Added: Keep Wealth above zero.
learning_goal: Does pushing for promotion and pay in quiet periods raise level and wealth enough to beat the survival-only F3 family, or does it add eliminations (health, trust crisis) that cancel the gain? This is the stagnation slot's contrarian question: is the F3 family too defensive when there are no warnings?
predicted_behaviour: Notes start with Recover, Secure, Repair or Grow. Before the first review and in quarters after B or better reviews without risk signals, the main action is Apply for a key project or Showcase results and Energy goes to High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials. After a risk signal, Defuse legacy risk in the next Energy phase. After a C or D, the main action follows the factor named until the next review. Compared with F3-family Haiku runs: more High-intensity work and key projects, fewer Network maintenance and Lay low quarters, more A grades in the second half of the run, a higher ending level and wealth, and a similar completion rate.
refutation: Refuted if, on 4 or more Haiku runs, posterior Y is not above f3-lean's and F3's, or completion falls below theirs, or the ending level and wealth dimensions are not higher than the F3 family's completed runs. Harmful if eliminations by health, burnout or trust crisis appear that F3-family runs did not show (Grow is then too aggressive; next step is a gentler Grow, not more rules). Manipulation fails if notes do not carry the mode or Grow quarters do not show key projects and High-intensity work; then the text is not executed and the run says nothing about the hypothesis.
notes: Seed of a new family requested by the strategy session after the score-gap analysis; it is also the stall response for the cloud run's first block (leader posterior mean 61.34 -> 60.21 over three decisions). No numbers, calendar triggers or event names in the Skill: grades S-D, the 0-10 range and action names are published; 'a whole quarter' and 'until the next review' use only the published cadence; 'Skill trails Output' compares two visible statistics. Parents list F3 and f3-lean as text sources only; the policy's family is new, so it does not use the F3 family's progressive-widening slots.
